title: Validator and Repair Effects Under Shared-Initial-Candidate Semantics: A Paired Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment that measured the effect of a deterministic validator and at-most-one repair on the same sampled model candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics) in an LLM-driven NetOps pipeline. The preregistered design targeted retrieval-augmentation (RAG) poisoning attacks, but the executed adapter disabled retrievals (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); therefore the realized estimand compares baseline single-shot validity of a shared sampled candidate against the final guarded (validator ± permitted repair) validity on that same candidate. On N = 250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 judged every sampled initial candidate valid (250/250), no repairs were applied, and baseline and guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rates were identical (1.0). Mapping the preregistered estimand actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms; paired difference = 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this execution; we document this deviation, quantify the power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈ 0.05 vs. observed 0.0), and discuss construct and external-validity limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, single deterministic validator, no RAG). All execution artifacts, preregistration, and analysis scripts are archived in the execution manifest.

sections.introduction: Motivation and question. Large language models (LLMs) are widely proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and staged change workflows. Because unconstrained LLM outputs can violate operational invariants (ordering, reachability, policy), guarded architectures that combine an LLM generator with deterministic validators and bounded repairs (generate→validate→repair) are commonly advocated. We preregistered candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 to test whether targeted poisoning of retrieval contexts (RAG) increases actionable-misconfiguration rates. The executed run, however, used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and retrieval_augmented_generation = false, so the empirical estimand realized by the run compares: (a) the validator result on the single sampled candidate (baseline) versus (b) the validator result after any permitted repair on that same candidate (guarded). This paper (1) reports the preregistered plan and the executed contract, (2) presents the artifact-backed confirmatory results under the executed semantics, (3) documents the preregistration deviation that prevented testing RAG-poisoning, and (4) discusses implications, threats to validity, and next steps.
sections.related_work: Surveys and recent application work document active interest in LLM-driven NetOps (intent decomposition, configuration generation, zero-touch automation) and motivate verifier- or tool-augmented architectures to reduce LLM-induced errors [1]–[5]. Evidence from NetOps-adjacent domains shows LLMs can produce factual errors, constraint violations, or adversarially exploitable outputs, motivating RAG and tool-planning mitigations [6]–[9]. Prior proposals integrate deterministic network verifiers and simulators as validators in LLM pipelines, but systematic, topology-grounded empirical measurements of guarded pipelines under adversarial retrievals remain an open gap motivating our preregistration [10]. (Cited items are the verified records archived with the execution bundle; the submission's References section lists full bibliographic metadata for each cited work.)
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and executed contract. The study was preregistered as candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 and executed under adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses). Key executed contract fields (artifact-backed): generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across baseline and guarded arms); retrieval_augmented_generation = false (no retrievals, hence no RAG/poisoning injection); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; task_count = 250; planned_episode_count = 500; completed_episode_count = 500; model_calls_used = 250. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset must not be interpreted as temperature = 0 and is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling. The exact initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

Estimand and operational mapping (explicit). The preregistration defined the primary estimand as the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate under poisoning (RAG) vs. clean retrievals. Because retrievals were disabled in execution, the realized estimand is different and must be stated explicitly:
- Preregistered primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_poisoned_minus_clean at poison_fraction = 0.30 (not realized; requires retrieval_augmented_generation = true).
- Executed (realized) estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, where each task yields exactly one sampled candidate reused by both conditions and guarded may apply deterministic validation±repair to that same candidate. Operationalization: archived VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 (validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5). We define actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. The paired test therefore compares the actionable_misconfig indicator for baseline (validator on shared initial candidate) versus guarded (final validator result after any permitted repair on the same candidate).

Experimental flow and analysis. For each of 250 tasks the adapter obtained one initial sample (shared). Baseline recorded the validator result on that candidate. Guarded executed the deterministic validator and, if violations were present, permitted at most one repair; the final guarded result is the validator outcome after any permitted repair. The primary confirmatory test is the paired comparison of actionable_misconfig indicators (exact McNemar two-sided test, α = 0.05). We computed a paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). All analysis used the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor and the archived result artifacts; specific analysis outputs referenced below are available in analysis/*.csv artifacts whose hashes are in the execution manifest.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed). The run started 2026-08-31T21:04:12Z and completed 2026-08-31T21:49:56Z. Planned episodes 500 (2×250) completed with zero failed episodes. Provider-call audit shows 250 hosted-model call events corresponding to the shared initial generation stage and zero further independent per-condition generation calls.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed and exact): The archived paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (all 250 pairs had VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1). Under actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION this yields zero actionable misconfigs in both arms. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode. Representative scoring examples and response traces (e.g., task-000004) show identical shared initial candidates across baseline and guarded arms; their file paths and hashes are archived in the execution manifest.

Preregistration deviation and power mismatch. The preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses required retrieval_augmented_generation = true and controlled poison injections; the executed adapter set retrieval_augmented_generation = false and performed no retrievals. Therefore the preregistered primary hypothesis was not testable in this run. Moreover, the preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline actionable-misconfig rate ≈ 0.05; the observed baseline rate was 0.0, invalidating the original sensitivity claims for RAG-poisoning detection and creating a power/assumption mismatch that we document and discuss below.
sections.discussion:
What the executed evidence supports. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics with a deterministic validator and retrieval disabled, the guarded pipeline did not change outcomes: the single sampled candidate reused across arms already satisfied validator checks for every task, so no repair or guard intervention occurred. The narrow, artifact-backed conclusion is: when baseline and guarded arms start from the same candidate that deterministic_netops_validator_v5 deems VALID_CONFIGURATION, the guarded pipeline produces no paired change in actionable-misconfiguration rate.

What it does not support. These results do not imply guarded pipelines are unnecessary in general. The experiment did not exercise retrieval-augmented generation, did not perform independent per-condition sampling (by design), used synthetic tasks and one model/validator, and therefore cannot adjudicate the originally preregistered RAG-poisoning hypotheses or generalize across production topologies, vendors, or alternative validators.

Validity threats. Internal validity: the archived provider and reconciliation artifacts confirm shared_initial_candidate semantics and one shared initial generation per task; this isolates validator/repair effects but precludes measuring independent-generation variability. Construct validity: the deterministic validator implements a rule set and may not capture all production failure modes (vendor-specific APIs, asynchronous state). External validity: synthetic task families, single LLM (gpt-5-mini), and single deterministic validator limit generalization. Conclusion validity: homogeneous outcomes produce tight within-run CIs that reflect the controlled corpus rather than operational heterogeneity.

Implications and next steps. To test the preregistered RAG/poisoning estimand requires enabling retrieval_augmented_generation, controlled poison fragments with provenance flags, and independent per-condition sampling (not shared_initial_candidate). Follow-up runs should broaden validators, include vendor-specific semantics, and diversify models. We preserve these as concrete future preregistration targets rather than retrofitting claims onto the present execution.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; retrieval disabled). The run produced 250/250 VALID_CONFIGURATION outcomes, no repairs were applied, and no actionable misconfigurations were observed in either arm (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). Crucially, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable because retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter; this preregistration deviation and the power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈ 0.05 vs. observed 0.0) limit confirmatory inference about retrieval-poisoning. Follow-up preregistered experiments that enable controlled retrieval augmentation and poisoning injection, broaden validator realism, and evaluate independent-generation semantics are necessary to measure guarded pipelines' mitigation potential under adversarial retrievals and sampling variability.

The human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the lock. Executed adapter and model: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter requesting gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses). Deterministic validator used: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Preregistration: candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 (preregistration manifest archived and sha256 referenced in execution manifest). The exact initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Executed adapter contract (artifact-backed) set generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across baseline and guarded arms) and retrieval_augmented_generation = false (no retrievals, hence no RAG/poisoning injection). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and must not be interpreted as temperature = 0. All raw outputs, validator traces, analysis scripts, paired contingency artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced by the submission.
limitations: The executed design used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across arms; it therefore measures validator/repair effects on the same candidate and cannot detect differences that require independent per-condition generation variability.

Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses and dose–response analyses were therefore not testable in this run and are recorded as a preregistration deviation.

The stored scorer semantics required explicit mapping to the preregistered estimand: archived VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 corresponds to no actionable misconfiguration, hence actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. This mapping was applied consistently in all reported analyses.

A single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used on synthetic tasks; these choices limit external validity to diverse production topologies, vendor semantics, and multi-model ensembles.

The model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling—hosted-model nondeterminism may remain and is logged in archived provider traces. The observed zero-event outcome (no actionable misconfigs) violates the preregistered baseline-rate assumption (≈0.05) and therefore does not constitute a sensitive test of the original poisoning hypothesis.
